steps.title: Expose energy created by the update
steps.explanation: Use the same 1 kg, 40 N/m spring starting at x = 0.20 m and v = 0. At h = 0.05 s, explicit Euler multiplies energy by 1 + 40h² = 1.1 each step. After 40 steps, t = 2 s and E = 0.8 × 1.1⁴⁰.
steps.observe: Energy grows to 36.2074 J, a maximum deviation of 4425.93%. Position is 1.27918 m, versus analytic 0.199316 m at the same 2 s.

steps.title: Change the update, preserve the experiment
steps.explanation: Keep the initial state, step size and 2 s endpoint. Updating velocity before position changes the numerical method. Its endpoint energy looks much closer, but inspect the maximum over every completed step rather than trusting a single snapshot.
steps.observe: Final energy is 0.766327 J, while maximum energy deviation is 18.7744%. Absolute position error is 0.00550736 m. Bounded-looking motion does not imply exact conservation.

steps.title: Use both endpoint accelerations
steps.explanation: Velocity Verlet uses old and new acceleration. The same 40 steps reach the same physical time. At this endpoint the energy happens to lie very near 0.8 J; the maximum over all samples prevents that phase coincidence from hiding error.
steps.observe: Final energy is 0.799632 J, but maximum energy deviation is 2.49928%. Position error is 0.00116381 m. These are measured numerical errors, not a conservation proof.

steps.title: Refine at equal elapsed time
steps.explanation: Reduce h fivefold and use five times as many steps so the endpoint remains 2 s. Comparing equal step counts here would compare different experiments. The finer run uses the same physical model and no retuned constants.
steps.observe: Maximum energy deviation falls to 0.0999895% and endpoint position error to 0.0000353055 m. Both improve in this experiment; this does not establish a universal error bound.

audit.finding: The embedded view reported only current energy and drift with a fixed step size. A near-zero endpoint drift could conceal much larger intermediate error.
audit.change: Added supported step sizes, analytic reference position and maximum relative energy deviation across every completed sample; worked comparisons match 2 s physical time.
audit.remaining: Ideal linear oscillator only; observed refinement is not a proof for arbitrary trajectories or biological systems. The full original lab retains longer traces and exports.
